name: Lead styphnate
description: Lead styphnate (CAS 15245-44-0 ), also known as lead trinitroresorcinate, is a primary explosive compound used as an initiating agent in energetic systems. It reliably converts a low-energy stimulus into a detonation signal. This material reacts to friction, heat, or electrostatic discharge, making it a foundational component in primer and ignition train design. In small arms and artillery ammunition, it is the active initiating compound in primer compositions. The compound generates the initial deflagration that ignites propellant charges. Defense and aerospace pyrotechnic assemblies rely on it within multi-component ignition trains to ensure consistent, low-threshold initiation across various conditions. In commercial and industrial detonators used in mining and demolition, it functions as the primary charge. It bridges the gap between an electrical or percussion stimulus and the secondary explosive for reliable performance. It is also incorporated into specialty squib and initiator devices used in aerospace safety systems, including ejection seats and airbag inflators. This versatility makes it essential for high-reliability safety and defense applications. Lead styphnate is supplied as a wetted powder or paste to reduce sensitivity during handling and transport. Normal lead styphnate and basic lead styphnate are the two commercially recognized forms available for industrial use. Each form has distinct initiation characteristics suited to different primer formulations. Material is typically produced and supplied to military specification grades and is subject to strict regulatory controls governing quantity and packaging. All shipments must comply with end-use authorization requirements.
